novelty_and_mechanism_assessment: The proposed vulnerability is fundamentally textbook negative transfer / gradient interference in multi-task shared-trunk architectures under asymmetric mask/loss conditions. Calling standard catastrophic cross-head backpropagation a novel 'security threat' or 'causal role privilege' rebranding does not elevate ordinary representation drift into a distinct threat model, particularly when the attacker is merely contributing standard (even truthful) training data within the intended distribution. The proposed defense ('stop_gradient' or decoupled trunks) is the standard ablation for multi-task gradient conflict.
minimum_decisive_next_experiment_using_p: Fine-tune the official pretrained FACT transformer on a poisoned batch of valid failure transitions (where action loss is masked out but true future/value targets are supervised) alongside clean replay data under standard multi-task balance (not toy 100x drift dynamics), and measure whether clean closed-loop policy performance drops significantly compared to standard multi-task fine-tuning without the adversary having to inject degenerate out-of-distribution value/future targets.
what_result_would_falsify_it: If under realistic pretraining/fine-tuning learning rates, optimizer states, and replay-buffer mixing ratios on the official FACT checkpoint, either: (1) the shared-prefix representations are robust enough that downstream action evaluation metrics (success rate, return) degrade by less than noise margins (<5%), or (2) the policy degradation is completely symmetric and non-exploitable (i.e., outcome prediction accuracy on clean states also collapses proportionally, reducing it to generic task interference rather than a stealthy backdoor/manipulation vector).
